rationale: Keep Durham Region Courthouse as a standalone operational infrastructure asset and reject the earlier conceptual-portfolio merge. INPP's and Amber's current official case studies each report 100% equity ownership, operational status, a March 2007 financial close and a 30-year term from construction completion. Infrastructure Ontario identifies Access Justice Durham as the DBFM consortium and confirms completion in 2009. Add the legal project-company alias, preserve the INPP-linked canonical manager name, record the officially disclosed 100% stake, improve the location and description, refresh milestone evidence, and make INPP's current project page the primary citation.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Durham Region Courthouse is an operational judicial public-private partnership in Oshawa, Ontario. Access Justice Durham Limited is responsible for the financing, maintenance and lifecycle renewal of the approximately 440,000-square-foot courthouse, which consolidates Superior Court and Ontario Court of Justice services in 33 courtrooms. Babcock & Brown Public Partnerships, INPP's predecessor, acquired 100% of the project-company equity at financial close in March 2007. INPP and Amber currently report 100% equity ownership and a 30-year term from construction completion; Infrastructure Ontario records construction completion in November 2009.

set.event: The project received an Award of Merit for Project Financing from the Canadian Council for Public-Private Partnerships.
